name: Convert unsignalized junction to single-lane roundabout
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Largest gains for injury crashes at rural and suburban junctions.

name: Convert signalized intersection to roundabout
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Severe-crash reduction dominates; rear-end crashes may rise slightly.

name: Install traffic signal at high-volume unsignalized junction
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Warrant analysis required; angle-crash benefit offsets rear-end increase.

name: Protected left-turn signal phasing
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Converts permissive lefts to protected-only at high-conflict approaches.

name: Leading pedestrian interval (LPI)
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: 3-7 s head start for pedestrians; near-zero capital cost.

name: Prohibit right turn on red at conflict-heavy approaches
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Applies where turning conflicts with crossings are documented.

name: Retro-reflective signal backplates
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Improves signal conspicuity including power-failure conditions.

name: Convert two-way stop to all-way stop control
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Suited to balanced approach volumes on local streets.

name: Add channelized left-turn lane at junction
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Removes turning queues from through lanes on major approaches.

name: Add right-turn lane at junction approach
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Approach-level treatment for high right-turning volumes.

name: Realign skewed intersection approaches
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Restores sight triangles at acute-angle rural junctions.

name: Advance junction warning signs on rural approaches
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Low-cost interim measure pending geometric upgrades.

name: Clear sight-distance obstructions at junction corners
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Vegetation and parking management within sight triangles.

name: Corridor signal coordination and retiming
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Smooths platoon progression; pair with speed management.

name: Red-light camera enforcement at signalized junction
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Angle-crash reduction; monitor rear-end trade-off.

name: Convert mini-roundabout at compact urban junction
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Compact footprint alternative where land take is constrained.

name: Raised intersection (full-plateau junction table)
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Speed-securing treatment for local and collector junctions.

name: Upgrade multi-lane roundabout to turbo-roundabout layout
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Eliminates lane-change conflicts inside the circulatory carriageway.

name: Raised pedestrian crossing
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Combines crossing priority with physical speed reduction.

name: Pedestrian refuge island at uncontrolled crossing
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Enables two-stage crossing on wide urban roads.

name: Pedestrian hybrid beacon (PHB/HAWK)
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Strongest uncontrolled-crossing treatment short of full signalization.

name: Rectangular rapid-flashing beacon (RRFB)
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: High driver-yielding gains at marked uncontrolled crossings.

name: Signalize marked zebra crossing on arterial
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: For arterials where zebra markings alone underperform.

name: Targeted lighting upgrade at pedestrian crossing
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Night-time pedestrian crash effect; verify uniformity not just lux.

name: Advance yield markings and signs before crossing
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Mitigates multiple-threat crashes on multilane approaches.

name: Curb extensions (build-outs) at crossing
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Shortens exposure and restores sight lines past parked cars.

name: Pedestrian countdown signal timers
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Retrofit to existing signal heads at signalized crossings.

name: Grade-separated pedestrian crossing (underpass/overpass)
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Only where desire lines can be served without detour non-compliance.

name: School-zone crossing package (signing marking patrols)
source: iRAP Safer Roads Toolkit
notes: Bundle of school-route treatments; pairs with 30 km/h zone.

name: Remove visual obstructions at crossing approaches
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Parking setbacks and street-furniture relocation near crossings.

name: Reduce speed limit from 50 to 30 km/h with supporting design
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Injury effect follows the speed-crash power model.

name: Fixed speed camera on high-speed urban arterial
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Localized effect around camera site (~1 km halo).

name: Average-speed (section) enforcement corridor
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Corridor-length compliance; stronger than spot cameras.

name: Speed humps on local street
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Local access streets only; check emergency-route conflicts.

name: Raised speed tables on collector street
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Flat-top profile compatible with buses and emergency vehicles.

name: Chicanes and horizontal deflection
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Alternating build-outs; preserve cycle through-routes.

name: Gateway treatment at town/village entry
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Signals urban-context transition on rural-to-urban approaches.

name: Vehicle-activated speed feedback signs
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Effective at curves junctions and school zones; effect decays without rotation.

name: Area-wide 30 km/h zone
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Neighbourhood-scale zone with self-explaining design.

name: Road diet (4-to-3 lane conversion)
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Frees space for cycle lanes and refuges; capacity check needed.

name: Lane narrowing with markings and median hatching
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Perceptual narrowing; verify cycle operating space is retained.

name: Transverse rumble strips on high-speed approach
source: iRAP Safer Roads Toolkit
notes: Alerting treatment before rural junctions and crossings; noise constraint in built-up areas.

name: Shoulder rumble strips
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Run-off-road crash countermeasure on rural mainline.

name: Centreline rumble strips on undivided rural road
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Head-on and opposite-direction sideswipe effect.

name: Median cable barrier on divided road
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Converts cross-median crashes to less severe barrier strikes.

name: Widen and pave shoulders
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Recovery space for drift-off errors on rural links.

name: Skid-resistant surfacing at high-friction-demand sites
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Targets wet-road and braking-zone crash clusters.

name: Realign substandard horizontal curve
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Geometric fix for out-of-context curves.

name: Curve warning signs with chevron alignment markers
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Delineation package for horizontal curves.

name: Correct curve superelevation deficiency
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Applies with resurfacing programmes.

name: High-friction surface treatment on curve or approach
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: One of the strongest wet-curve treatments in the Clearinghouse.

name: Convert to 2+1 road with median barrier
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Fatal-crash effect from continuous median separation.

name: Protected (kerb-separated) cycle lane
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Physical separation on arterials; junction treatment must accompany.

name: Painted cycle lane on urban street
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Weak stand-alone effect; use where speeds and volumes are low.

name: Relocate mid-block bus stops to laybys or boarders
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Removes stopping conflicts from the running lane.

name: Edge line and centreline marking refresh programme
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Maintenance-grade delineation baseline.

name: Install continuous road lighting on unlit section
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Night-crash effect; strongest for pedestrian night crashes.

name: Upgrade lighting to LED with uniformity compliance
source: EU RISM Directive 2019/1936
source_ref: Annex III indicative element 2(e) — visibility and lighting
notes: Uniformity and glare control per EN 13201 lighting classes.

name: Junction-specific lighting at rural intersection
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Isolated junction lighting on otherwise unlit rural links.

name: Tunnel lighting and transition-zone upgrade
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Adaptation-zone luminance per tunnel-lighting standards.

name: Install guardrail at high-severity roadside hazard
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Severity reduction for run-off-road crashes into fixed hazards.

name: Crash cushions at rigid obstacles (gore areas piers)
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Impact attenuators at unremovable point hazards.

name: Clear-zone widening and obstacle removal
source: iRAP Safer Roads Toolkit
notes: Forgiving roadside per iRAP star-rating drivers.

name: Replace rigid poles with passively-safe (breakaway) supports
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Passively safe supports per EN 12767 classes.

name: Protect or manage tree lines close to carriageway
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Barrier protection preferred over removal where trees are protected.

name: Relocate utility poles away from edge of carriageway
source: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse
notes: Increase lateral offset to 3 m or more.

name: Flatten side slopes / embankment regrading
source: Elvik et al. Handbook of Road Safety Measures (2009)
notes: Recoverable slopes reduce rollover likelihood.

name: Motorcycle-friendly barrier retrofit (rub-rail)
source: EU RISM Directive 2019/1936
source_ref: Annex III indicative element 2(d) — roadside protection for vulnerable users
notes: Under-run protection on curve barriers with motorcycle history.
